investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent record, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three failing checks (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized or the affinity rules are overly restrictive, capacity will exhaust under normal load.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may not have released VM resources (e.g., cleanup failed), reducing available capacity over time. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned VMs.

Quaternary — cluster autoscaler not provisioning additional kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured but new nodes take longer than the eval timeout (warningLatencyMs=240000, outageLatencyMs=360000 per features.json line 183), the eval will always fail during scale-out events.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent record, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 144s, zero evidence keys — confirms the capacity problem persisted across a third independent probe attempt.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized or the affinity rules are overly restrictive, capacity will exhaust under normal load.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user sessions may not have released VM resources (e.g., cleanup failed), reducing available capacity over time. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned VMs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-27 because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler. The scheduler message is consistent across all three checks: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and preventing any remote agent VM from starting.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The other 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never produced a running agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266-270 was entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no allocatable slots for new eval probe pods.

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive, targeting only 2 of 6 nodes, so even if total cluster VM capacity exists it is unreachable by these pods.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may not have completed), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and starving subsequent scheduling attempts.

Lower confidence: A cluster scaling event (node removal, node NotReady, or resource quota change) reduced the effective kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes between the time the eval was last passing and this run. No historical pass data is available (lastPassingAt is null) to bound the regression window.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available (non-zero) kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission error would need to be identified.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks passed in a subsequent run without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient scheduling contention rather than sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the pod spec for remote agents does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the scheduler message would indicate a misconfiguration in the node resource advertisement rather than true capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the root cause would be localized to the runtime check's pod spec or timing rather than a cluster-wide VM capacity issue.

If user-traffic metrics showed remote agent provisioning succeeding for end users during the same window, the failure would be scoped to the eval probe's service account, namespace, or quota rather than the shared VM pool.
